Yichang|China.f: Yichang is home to the Three Gorges Dam, the world's largest hydroelectric power station.

Qionghai|China.f: The town of Bo'ao in Qionghai is the permanent seat of the Boao Forum for Asia.

Xiahe|China.f: A hominin fossil jaw, the Xiahe mandible, was found in Baishiya Karst Cave in Xiahe County in 1980.

Yangzhou|China.f: In 1280 a fire at the Weiyang arsenal in Yangzhou set off a huge gunpowder explosion that killed over a hundred guards.

Jiuzhaigou|China.f: Jiuzhaigou literally means Nine Settlement Valley, after the nine Tibetan villages along its length.

Hotan|China.f: Silkworm eggs were smuggled out of Khotan, today's Hotan, to Iran and reached Constantinople in 551.

Linyi|China.f: Sun Tzu's Art of War was found on hand-written bamboo slips in Linyi in 1972, along with other classics.

Delingha|China.f: The name Delingha comes from Mongolian and means golden world.

Jinchang|China.f: Jinchang is known as China's Nickel Capital and also has deposits of copper, cobalt, gold and tungsten.

Yan'an|China.f: Around 1080 the scholar Shen Kuo found petrified bamboo near Yan'an and deduced the region's climate was once much wetter.

Zhangye|China.f: Kublai Khan is said to have been born at Dafo Temple in Zhangye, home to China's longest wooden reclining Buddha.

Nyingchi|China.f: Nyingchi's airport is the only one in the world where every takeoff and landing must follow RNP AR procedures.

Shache|China.f: Yarkant, now Shache, was the capital of the Yarkent Khanate from 1514 until its fall in 1713.

Shaoguan|China.f: In the 1950s farmers near Shaoguan found a partial skull of Maba Man, an early East Asian hominid.

Chengde|China.f: Chengde's Putuo Zongcheng Temple, loosely modeled on the Potala in Lhasa, was finished in just four years in 1771.

Erenhot|China.f: Iren Dabasu, the salt lake near Erenhot, is known to paleontologists for yielding many different dinosaurs.

Manzhouli|China.f: Manzhouli has a border tourist area with a hotel shaped like a giant matryoshka doll.

Xilinhot|China.f: Xilinhot was long known as Beizi Temple, after a temple the Qianlong Emperor built there in 1743.

Shennongjia|China.f: Shennongjia has the highest diversity of deciduous woody plant species in the world.

Guyuan|China.f: According to the History of Yuan, Genghis Khan died in the Liupan Mountains near Guyuan in 1227.

Longnan|China.f: Longnan is considered the homeland of the House of Ying, the family of the Qin dynasty that united China.

Tianshui|China.f: Near Tianshui, the Maijishan Grottoes hold thousands of Buddhist sculptures made between the Wei and Song dynasties.

Yulin (Shaanxi)|China.f: Lake Hongjiannao, on the edge of Yulin, is China's largest desert freshwater lake.

Zhongwei|China.f: The Tengger Desert Solar Park near Zhongwei is one of the world's largest photovoltaic power stations.

Anqing|China.f: The name Anqing was created in 1147 by combining the last characters of two older names, Tong'an and Deqing.

Dongying|China.f: The Shengli Oil Field in the Yellow River delta around Dongying, found in 1961, is China's second-largest oil field.

Jining|China.f: Liangshan, a county of Jining, is the main setting of the classic novel Water Margin.

Wuhu|China.f: Wuhu is known for wrought iron pictures, a craft folklore credits to an itinerant blacksmith named Tang Tianchi.

Anshun|China.f: Huangguoshu Waterfall, 45 km from Anshun, is described as the biggest waterfall in Asia.

Panzhihua|China.f: Panzhihua held 93 percent of China's titanium reserves at the end of 2007, the world's largest deposit.

Zunyi|China.f: The 1935 Zunyi Conference, held during the Long March, elevated Mao Zedong to a dominant position in the Communist Party.

Qiemo|China.f: Several mummies, including Cherchen Man, were found near Qiemo, known in the West as Cherchen.

Ruoqiang|China.f: Ruoqiang County covers 199,222 square km, making it the largest county-level division in China.

Turpan|China.f: Ayding Lake in the Turpan Basin lies 154 m below sea level.

Korla|China.f: Korla is known for fragrant pears and is the headquarters of PetroChina's Tarim oil field operations.

Tongren|China.f: The nature reserve around Tongren is the only natural habitat of the endangered Guizhou snub-nosed monkey.

Holingol|China.f: Holingol is a county-level city of about 70,000 people that includes 17 ethnic groups.

Xinyang|China.f: Jingju Temple in Xinyang's Guangshan county is cited as the source of the first Chinese section of Tiantai Buddhism, in 554.

Luzhou|China.f: A baijiu fermentation pit in Luzhou, commissioned in 1573, has reportedly been in continuous operation ever since.

Bazhong|China.f: From 1933 to 1935 the Red Army's Fourth Front Army ran a Soviet government in Bazhong in Sichuan-Shaanxi Province.
